look_up_product.description: Turn a barcode into a product: its name, brand, model, category, pictures, and what the shops UPCitemdb tracks are charging, cheapest in stock first. Takes the number printed under the bars (a UPC, an EAN, a GTIN or a book's ISBN) or an Amazon ASIN, and works out which it is. The short barcode on a small package is expanded and an old 10-digit ISBN is converted, so the code you actually have is the code that works. A barcode nobody has comes back as not found rather than as an error, so a workflow can branch on it.

search_products.description: Find products by name when you don't have a barcode, and get their barcodes back. Search the whole catalogue or just books, narrow it by brand, category, model number or a word in the title, and choose whether every word has to appear or the closest matches will do. Each result is the same full product record a barcode lookup returns, prices and pictures included. Worth knowing: searching is limited more tightly than looking a barcode up on UPCitemdb's free plan, so a search-heavy workflow is the first reason to add a key.

description: Turn a barcode into a product. UPCitemdb holds records for around 735 million barcodes (what the thing is, who makes it, what it looks like, and what the shops it tracks are charging), so a scan, a supplier's spreadsheet or a stock take can be filled in without anyone typing a product name. Look up one code or a whole column of them, or search by name when you don't have a code at all. Free to use with no account; add an API key when you need a bigger daily allowance.
